entry.title: 3 RRC message traps I keep seeing in 5G NR drive tests (and how to spot them)
entry.summary: RRC traces look simple on the surface. You decode a few messages, you read the field names, and you think you understand what the UE and the gNB are doing. Then you spend half a day chasing a bug that was never really a bug. Three scenarios come back in almost every 5G NR drive test I analyze. Each one is easy to misread if you look at the message in isolation. You see an RRCReconfiguration in the trace, you open it, and the measConfig section is empty or only has a measObjectToRemoveList. First reaction of many engineers : "the network just dropped the measurement setup, that is why we lost the neighbor". Most of the time that conclusion is wrong.
